cases.description: When the versionFlag argument is null the method should return null (first guard clause).
Enum constant V202012 should map to a new instance of Version202012.
Enum constant V201909 should map to a new instance of Version201909.
Enum constant V7 should map to a new instance of Version7.
Enum constant V6 should map to a new instance of Version6.
Enum constant V4 should map to a new instance of Version4.

If a future/unsupported enum constant is passed (not covered by the switch cases), the method must throw IllegalArgumentException (default branch). In the test a mock enum value is created via reflection to simulate this scenario.
When versionFlag is V202012 the method should return a non‑null object whose runtime class is com.networknt.schema.Version202012.
When versionFlag is V201909 the method should return a non‑null object whose runtime class is com.networknt.schema.Version201909.
When versionFlag is V7 the method should return a non‑null object whose runtime class is com.networknt.schema.Version7.
When versionFlag is V6 the method should return a non‑null object whose runtime class is com.networknt.schema.Version6.
When versionFlag is V4 the method should return a non‑null object whose runtime class is com.networknt.schema.Version4.
Calling checkVersion(V202012) twice must produce two different instances (no caching), i.e., the references are not equal.
Calling checkVersion(V201909) twice must produce two different instances.
Calling checkVersion(V7) twice must produce two different instances.
Calling checkVersion(V6) twice must produce two different instances.
Calling checkVersion(V4) twice must produce two different instances.

When an enum constant that is not handled by the switch (e.g., a mock constant named UNSUPPORTED) is supplied, the method must throw IllegalArgumentException and the exception message must include the string representation of the unsupported value.
